scope: Independent read-only review of the sealed 46-claim Machine Metrics proposal. It checks frozen baseline/model binding, source and selector integrity, proposed replacement locality, and whether the 18 corrections keep their claims proportionate to the cited evidence.

plan.baseline_binding: Recompute every frozen claim object's equality with the pinned Git model, its literal hash, and its exact original source span.
plan.evidence_binding: Recompute every staged-source hash and resolve every declared source selector to its retained excerpt; inspect the current UI observations only within their stated account, machine, date, and display limits.
plan.replacement_review: Apply the 18 proposed replacements in memory only and verify that no other baseline line or Markdown table shape changes. Review each replacement against its cited product, engineering, primary-definition, or bounded UI evidence.
plan.safety: Read-only local artifact and immutable-Git inspection. No Host, account, hardware, browser, daemon, rental, network, documentation, model, graph, or source retrieval operation was performed.

results.observation: All 46 inventory IDs match the decisions IDs and the pinned model. Each original literal hash and one-line source span matches commit 36d2945482f18cb2995be466dbdce1ecc592a62e. The sealed decision and source-index hashes match their declared target values.

All 19 staged-source hashes match their index entries and all 160 exact selectors resolve byte-for-byte to their declared excerpts. The preserved retrieval records distinguish the initial failed retrieval and the later retained source capture; the unbound SwapTotal selector remains explicitly not used as proof.

The retained, read-only Host-team observations support the currently visible Machine selector, metric controls, device grids, Reset, timeline/run zoom, UTC display, and a no-data row. They do not establish sampling accuracy, collection timing, retention, outage recovery, hardware health, or fault causation; the decisions preserve those limits.

The corrections retain safe bounds for lag and local-buffer recovery; Linux load, memory, swap, I/O-wait, and steal interpretations; GPU utilization and clock-event qualifiers; network counter attribution; timeline and row-detail limits; and troubleshooting advice. None turns a counter, visual pattern, or UI control into a guarantee of a hardware fault, crash loop, oversubscription, or workload cause.

An in-memory application changes exactly lines 19, 24, 29, 51, 70, 77, 81, 98, 100, 117, 128, 138, 141, 148, 149, 150, 152, and 153 of host/machine-metrics.mdx. The other 142 baseline lines and all selected table column counts are preserved.

residual_limits: This is source and bounded-display evidence, not a live hardware, daemon, workload, retention, or failure-reproduction qualification.
The retained UI context is one authorized Host team manager and one selected four-GPU machine on its recorded date; it is not a universal console contract.
The original engineer-approved publication establishes provenance but does not convert unsupported runtime behavior into verified fact.
Root retains the acceptance and integration decision; this review does not modify the original documentation, model, or graph.
recommendation: The sealed Metrics46 proposal is source-consistent, proportionately qualified, and ready for root acceptance and integration review.
